bull.b: Strong multi‑billion operating cash flow (~$23.2B TTM) and free cash flow (~$13.4B TTM) enhance GM's ability to fund capex, EV investments, buybacks and debt paydown. Durable cash generation provides a financial cushion through cycles and supports strategic execution over the medium term.

Dominant U.S. full‑size pickup share (>42%) and record fleet deliveries give GM durable advantages in its most profitable segment. Scale in trucks underpins pricing power, fixed‑cost absorption and dealer relationships that help sustain margins and cash flow through cyclical downturns.

Growing digital subscriptions, deferred revenue ($6.3B) and rising recognized digital revenue ($800M) create higher‑margin, recurring income. As the installed base and ADAS attach rates expand, software monetization can sustainably raise per‑vehicle economics and lifetime customer value.

bear.b: Debt‑to‑equity near 2.0x signals elevated leverage for a cyclical automaker, constraining financial flexibility to fund investments or absorb shocks. Higher leverage raises refinancing and interest risk and reduces optionality for sustained multi‑year investments in EV scale and onshoring.

Cumulative $10.9B EV restructuring charges, with a ~$7.2B cash impact, reflect costly program right‑sizings and impairments tied to the EV transition. These material, programmatic costs can pressure near‑term cash and delay achieving sustainable EV profitability despite future scale benefits.

Gross margin compression to ~6.1% TTM (from ~17.4% in 2024) and EBIT margin near ~1.3% TTM indicate persistent profitability pressure from costs, mix and pricing. Sustained margin weakness reduces internal funding for launches, onshoring and EV investments and heightens sensitivity to volume and commodity swings.
